title: Where you are and what is here

terminal.description: A shell that starts in the studio's folder. Type a command, press Enter and read what it prints.

tasks.title: Write down where the terminal starts
tasks.description:
Find out which folder the terminal is in when it opens, and write its full path after `here:` in `notes.txt`.

A full path starts with `/` and names every folder from the top of the computer down to this one.

Check compares your line with the folder the terminal opens in for this issue.
nextSteps: Click in the terminal so you can type in it.
Run the command from the lesson that prints where you are.
Copy the whole line it prints.
hints: The lesson's part about where you are names a command of three letters.
`pwd` prints one line, the full path of the folder you are in. That whole line is the answer.
Run `pwd`, select the line it prints, copy it, and paste it after `here:` so the line reads `here: /...`.

videos.title: Moving around the terminal with pwd, ls and cd

tasks.title: Find the biggest artwork file
tasks.description:
Idris says one file in `artwork` is so big it keeps filling the memory stick. List `artwork` with sizes and write the name of its biggest file after `biggest:` in `notes.txt`, exactly as `ls` shows it.

The file panel does not show sizes, so this one needs the terminal.

Check compares your answer with the file in `artwork` that has the most bytes.
nextSteps: List what is in `artwork`, by giving `ls` the folder's name.
Ask `ls` for the long listing, which has a size column.
Find the biggest number in that column.
Write that file's whole name after `biggest:`.
hints: The plain listing only shows names. The lesson shows an option that adds a size to each line.
`-l` gives the long listing. The size in bytes is the number just before the date.
Run `ls -l artwork`, find the line with the largest size, and copy the name at the end of that line.

tasks.title: Find the hidden handover note
tasks.description:
Sol, who used to help on Saturdays, left a handover note in `desk`, but it does not show up in the file panel or in a plain listing. Find it and write its name after `hidden:` in `notes.txt`, exactly as `ls` shows it.

Check compares your answer with the names of the hidden files in `desk`.
nextSteps: List `desk` the plain way and see what shows.
Ask `ls` to show every name, hidden ones too.
Find the name that was not there before.
Write it after `hidden:`, with every character it has.
hints: Some names are left out of a listing on purpose. The lesson says which ones and how to see them.
`ls -a` shows all names. Hidden names start with a dot, and the dot belongs to the name.
Run `ls -a desk`. Leave out `.` and `..`, and the name that remains is the answer.
